subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers replace the conflicting fork PR with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, adopt and refresh that fork PR, or defer this bug to broader title-quality work?
rationale: The bug shape is clear and source-reproducible, but an open fork PR already uses closing syntax and is conflicting without maintainer edit access, so automation should not create a competing fix PR until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the fork branch and land a same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async display-name hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing proof and coverage, then review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Defer To Broader Title Work
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for the broader session-title direction before changing the current fallback chain.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the fork branch and land a same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async display-name hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter committed the original session picker work and has recent Gateway session-list history, making this the best available owner for the adopt-versus-replace decision.
